Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

intense adjective

also intensely, intensity, fierce, strong (of a feeling, heat or pain), violent (of pain, wind), noble (sentiments)

classical

Plin. NH 24.62: dolor capitis vehementior (Lewis & Short)
Lucr. 6.517: imber (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 17.235: vīs frīgorum aut calōrum (Lewis & Short)

vehemēns, vehementis

adjective, third declension, one ending

intense, strong, violent

Of pain, rain, heat, cold, a blow or a feeling: strong, powerful; of a person, vehement, violent. The adverb vehementer is the everyday “very much, intensely” (vehementer gaudeō).

Other words

  • ācer, ācris, ācre — sharp, keen, fierce

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.183: ācer et vehemēns incitātiō (Lewis & Short, s.v. vehemēns)

    Sharp to the senses (a piercing cold, a pungent taste), keen in mind, fierce in battle; intense in that it bites.

  • intentus, intenta, intentum — intent, strained (of attention)

    also used · classical · Cic. Fl. 11 (Lewis & Short, s.v. intendō): quam maximē intentīs … oculīs contemplārī; Verg. A. 2.1: intentī ōra tenēbant (Lewis & Short)

    Intense attention or effort: intentus with the dative or ablative of what one is intent on; intentissima cūra, the most intense care (Quint.).

  • grandis, grande — great, strong (of feelings); lofty (of sentiments)

    also used · classical · Traupman 155, 156

    Properly “full-grown, large”.

Examples

  • cōnsonant vehementer, proinde ut mīlitēs faciunt, cum castra movent

    they hum loudly, just as soldiers do when they break campVarr. RR 3.16.30

  • Aspiciō intentīs oculīs.

    I’m watching with all my attention.Corderius, Coll. II 46 (sixteenth century)

See also strong, severe.
